detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 4.1 Describing Motion and Equations of Kinematics
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Kinematics uses reference frames to quantify displacement, velocity v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2, and v^2 - u^2 = 2as.

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: Shortest distance from initial to final position with direction.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: First Equation of Motion
formulas_rules_and_laws.variable_definitions: v=final velocity, u=initial velocity, a=acceleration, t=time

m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.activity_or_procedure_title: Plotting Distance-Time Graph on an Inclined Track
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.objective_or_aim: Determine acceleration of a marble on a ramp.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.expected_observations_or_working: Parabolic curve indicating non-linear distance increase over time.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.scientific_or_logical_conclusion: Slope of position-time graph gives instantaneous velocity.

diagrams_and_illustrations.figure_title: Velocity-Time Graph for Uniformly Accelerated Motion
diagrams_and_illustrations.drawing_or_labeling_instructions: Plot velocity on y-axis, time on x-axis; draw straight inclined line.
diagrams_and_illustrations.key_structural_details: Slope equals acceleration a; area of trapezoid equals displacement s.

scripted_dialogues.speech_text: Can an object have a constant speed but non-zero acceleration?

scripted_dialogues.speaker: Student
scripted_dialogues.speech_text: Yes! In uniform circular motion, the speed is constant, but the direction of velocity changes continuously, producing a centripetal acceleration toward the center.
